title: Restriction triangle inside a closed support
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, let $B,C\subseteq T$ be
closed subschemes, and
put $V=T\setminus C$, with open immersion $v:V\hookrightarrow T$.
Let $F$ be a bounded-below complex of module sheaves on the
small etale site.
Write $R\Gamma_B(T,F)$ for the derived functor of the
sections supported on $B$,
whose cohomology is the
cohomology with support.
There is a natural distinguished triangle in the
derived category of modules:

$$
R\Gamma_{B\cap C}(T,F)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_B(T,F)
\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{B\cap V}(V,v^*F)\longrightarrow
R\Gamma_{B\cap C}(T,F)[1].
$$

The third support is closed in $V$; its ambient scheme is $V$.

proof.text: Write $R$ for the fixed commutative coefficient ring and $W=T\setminus B$. For any closed support $Z\subset X$ put $\Gamma_Z(X,M)=\ker(M(X)\to M(X\setminus Z))$; this is an additive left exact functor of $R$-module sheaves, since kernels and sections preserve kernels. The module-sheaf categories on $T$ and $V$ have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. By [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], represent $F$ by a bounded-below complex $I^\bullet$ of injectives. The inverse image $v^*$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and it preserves injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives], since $v$ is open, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Thus $v^*I^\bullet=I^\bullet|_V$ represents $v^*F$ and is again bounded below with injective terms. Here restriction on sections is the one described in [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction].

source.place: Tags 013K (lemma-injective-resolutions-exist), 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective); enough injectives: injectives.tex, Tag 01DU (theorem-sheaves-modules-injectives); restriction input: sites-modules.tex, Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero) and 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact); open immersions: morphisms.tex, Tag 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale)

proof.text: Let $O=V\cup W=T\setminus(B\cap C)$ and $a:O\hookrightarrow T$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] to the pair $(B\cap C,O)$ and the constant rank-one module sheaf $R_T$. Its counit $a_!a^{-1}R_T\to R_T$ is a monomorphism. For every injective module sheaf $J$, the lifting property in [def-sp-injective-resolutions] makes precomposition with this monomorphism surjective. Under [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] this is precisely the restriction $J(T)\to J(O)$: a map $R_X\to M$ is determined by the image of $1$, and conversely a section $s\in M(X)$ gives the module map $r\mapsto r\,s|_{X'}$ on each etale $X'\to X$. The coefficient identification $a^{-1}R_T=R_O$ and agreement of module pullback with inverse image are supplied by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Hence $J(T)\to J(O)$ is surjective.

For $s\in\Gamma_{B\cap V}(V,J|_V)$, its restriction to $V\cap W$ is zero. The sheaf equalizer axiom in [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], applied to the open covering $O=V\cup W$, glues $s$ on $V$ and $0$ on $W$ to $t\in J(O)$. It applies to the underlying abelian sheaf of a module sheaf by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Lift $t$ to $\widetilde t\in J(T)$ by step 2. Then $\widetilde t|_W=0$, so $\widetilde t\in\Gamma_B(T,J)$, and $\widetilde t|_V=s$. This proves surjectivity of the required supported restriction without any assertion that the subsheaf of supported sections is injective.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: explicit extension of supported sections, using the open cover V union (T minus B)

proof.text:
The supported restriction has kernel $\Gamma_{B\cap C}(T,J)$. Indeed, a global section in its kernel vanishes on $W$ and on $V$, hence on $W\cup V=T\setminus(B\cap C)$ by the uniqueness part of the same sheaf equalizer axiom [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]; conversely vanishing on this union implies vanishing on each open. The left map is the inclusion of these kernels. Apply this and step 3 to every $J=I^m$. Restrictions commute with the differential, so one obtains a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes of $R$-modules
$$0\longrightarrow\Gamma_{B\cap C}(T,I^\bullet)\longrightarrow\Gamma_B(T,I^\bullet)\longrightarrow\Gamma_{B\cap V}(V,I^\bullet|_V)\longrightarrow0.$$
All maps here are inclusions or restrictions, and therefore commute with every map of complexes.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: kernel of restriction and resulting short exact sequence of section complexes

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], the first two complexes in step 4 compute respectively $R\Gamma_{B\cap C}(T,F)$ and $R\Gamma_B(T,F)$, since step 1 supplies a bounded-below injective representative. Apply the same result on $V$ to $I^\bullet|_V$, which is a bounded-below complex of injectives by step 1: the third complex computes $R\Gamma_{B\cap V}(V,v^*F)$. The support $B\cap V$ is closed in $V$ because it is the intersection of the closed subset $B$ of $T$ with $V$; sections supported there mean exactly the kernel of restriction to $V\cap W$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle], in the abelian category of $R$-modules, turns the short exact sequence of step 4 into the displayed distinguished triangle. The first two maps are precisely support inclusion and restriction.

source.place: Tags 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived), part (2), and 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic), part (1), for bounded-below injective computation; Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor) for the triangle

proof.text: To verify naturality, represent a morphism $F\to F'$ by a chain map between bounded-below injective representatives, using [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] and the K-injectivity clause of [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Step 4 gives a morphism of the short exact sequences. The naturality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] gives a morphism of their distinguished triangles, including the connecting arrow. Each of the three section functors is additive and carries a chain homotopy $h$ to a chain homotopy, since $f-g=dh+hd$ remains that equality after applying sections, restriction, or the support kernels. Thus homotopic representatives give identical morphisms of triangles. The Hom bijection in [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] also makes different injective representatives homotopy equivalent. Applying the preceding argument to those equivalences identifies the triangles and their connecting arrows. This proves the stated naturality on the derived category, independently of all resolution and lifting choices.

source.place: Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), (1) implies (3), for the Hom bijection; Tag 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective); Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), naturality of the connecting map

lean.note: The recorded supportRestrictionTriangle provides existence of a natural boundary but no normalization on injective-complex representatives. The comparison theorem needs the actual connecting map of the supported short exact sequence. This module retains the existing theorem by import and adds canonical support inclusion and open restriction, their short exact complex, and a uniquely normalized derived boundary. It also gives the canonical derived-composite comparison, actual support transport along open immersions, and the distinguished localization triangle; its D+ specialization is identified by rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility. The closed intersection and open supports are actual fibre products.
